prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_G:
Summary of 2019 manifesto proposals (neutral, non‑ideological)

Constitution and Europe
- Seek a legally undisputed referendum on Scottish independence by transferring the necessary powers to the Scottish Parliament.
- Support a UK‑wide second EU referendum with “Remain” on the ballot; back revoking Article 50 if the only alternative is no‑deal.
- Prioritise the closest possible relationship with the EU, including single market and customs union access.

Health and social care
- Call for UK health spending per head to match Scotland’s level, raising Scotland’s allocation via consequentials.
- Introduce an NHS Protection Act to exclude health services from trade deals and protect public ownership and commissioning.
- Secure compensation for the contaminated blood scandal.

Economy, tax and cost of living
- End austerity and reverse real‑terms cuts to Scotland’s budget; invest in public services and productivity.
- Crack down on tax avoidance/evasion; reform Companies House and improve transparency; review IR35 and loan charge issues.
- Freeze VAT and National Insurance rates; remove VAT from sanitary products and e‑publications; reform energy billing with a free national switching service and tariff clarity/caps.

Work, migration and rights
- Devolve employment law; raise the statutory living wage to at least the real Living Wage and end age differentials; strengthen action on the gender pay gap and gig‑economy rights.
- Devolve immigration powers to create a tailored system (including a Scottish Visa); reduce costs/complexity of citizenship; end indefinite detention; expand family reunion; allow asylum seekers to work.

Social security and pensions
- End the benefit freeze, sanctions regime, Universal Credit rollout (pending major reform), the bedroom tax, and the two‑child limit.
- Uprate income‑replacement benefits by at least inflation and run a UK‑wide benefit take‑up campaign.
- Protect the State Pension triple lock; oppose rises in State Pension age; restore Pension Credit changes; retain free TV licences for over‑75s.

Drugs policy and justice
- Devolve drugs legislation to pilot supervised drug consumption facilities; treat drug deaths as a public health emergency.
- Maintain cross‑border security cooperation tools with the EU.

Education and families
- Expand early learning and childcare; continue closing the attainment gap; retain free higher education.
- Overhaul parental leave: longer, better‑paid maternity, paternity and shared leave; neonatal leave; stronger redundancy protections.

Climate, energy and transport
- Meet statutory targets: net zero by 2045 (carbon neutral by 2040), 75% emissions cut by 2030.
- Green tax incentives (home energy efficiency, low‑carbon heat, zero‑emission vehicles); large‑scale tree planting.
- Decarbonise rail by 2035; major bus priority investment; support EV uptake; trial low/zero‑emission regional aviation.
- Accelerate carbon capture, utilisation and storage; create a Net Zero Fund from oil and gas receipts with support for affected regions.
- Expand renewables; allow onshore wind/solar into CfD auctions; reform grid charges; deliver island interconnectors; oppose new nuclear and fracking.

Infrastructure, digital and sectors
- Increase capital borrowing limits; grow the Scottish National Investment Bank; ensure fair shares of UK infrastructure and broadband/5G funds; social tariffs for connectivity.
- Support tourism (including examining a hospitality VAT cut), creative industries, and devolved broadcasting powers.

Rural economy, food and fisheries
- Secure full agricultural replacement funding and convergence uplift; protect food standards and geographical indications; compensate sectors hit by tariffs.
- Ensure fair treatment in supply chains; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator.
- Safeguard fisheries interests in access and annual negotiations; ensure equal standards for all vessels in Scottish waters.

Consumers and communities
- Strengthen consumer protections (caps on high‑cost credit, ticket bots ban, fair rural delivery charges); preserve access to cash and post offices; tackle gambling‑related harm; regulate online harms with a statutory duty of care and an independent regulator.

Defence, veterans and foreign policy
- Cancel the UK nuclear weapons system and redirect spending to public services.
- Retain bases and regiments; improve veterans’ housing and benefits; use vacant MoD homes for homeless veterans.
- Maintain 0.7% of GNI on international development; establish climate justice funding; tighten arms‑export controls; oppose lethal autonomous weapons.

Democracy and rights
- Replace first‑past‑the‑post with STV; abolish the unelected second chamber; extend voting to 16–17‑year‑olds and all lawful residents; create an independent debates commission.
- Protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; incorporate UNCRC; strengthen anti‑discrimination measures.

TEXT_D:
Summary of 2019 UK policy proposals (max 500 words)

- Europe and constitutional reform
  - Revoke Article 50 to remain in the EU if winning a majority; otherwise back a referendum with an option to remain.
  - Protect freedom of movement; enfranchise long‑term EU residents in UK elections; reform electoral registration to automatic inclusion.
  - Electoral reform to Single Transferable Vote for MPs and councils; votes at 16; overseas constituencies; House of Lords reform; stricter transparency and regulation of political advertising and lobbying; citizens’ assemblies on major issues.
  - Devolution to nations and English regions with a written federal constitution and matched funding powers.

- Economy, business and work
  - £130bn infrastructure plan (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing), plus a £50bn regional rebalancing programme and Green Investment Bank.
  - Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand Catapult centres; regional innovation funds; support creative industries.
  - Skills Wallets of £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning; broaden apprenticeship levy to a Skills and Training Levy.
  - Corporate governance reforms: employee board representation; due‑diligence duties on human rights/environment; binding shareholder votes on executive pay.
  - Tax: restore Corporation Tax to 20%; replace Business Rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; align capital gains with income tax; tougher anti‑avoidance and improved Digital Services Tax.
  - Work: new “dependent contractor” status with core rights; living wage approach; flexible working from day one; stronger enforcement; fair gig‑economy pensions and zero‑hours protections.

- Education and childcare
  - Free, high‑quality childcare: 35 hours/week, 48 weeks/year for ages 2–4 and from 9–24 months for working parents; increased early years funding and staff training; expanded Children’s Centres.
  - Reverse school funding cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; clear repairs backlog.
  - Replace SATs and narrow league tables with broader assessment; new inspectorate; stronger SEND funding.
  - “Curriculum for life,” arts protection, careers links, better vocational routes.
  - Further/higher education: +£1bn for colleges, restore maintenance grants, stronger student mental health, review finance; Young People’s Premium.

- Environment, energy and transport
  - Net‑zero by 2045; at least 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking.
  - Ten‑year nationwide home insulation and zero‑carbon heat programme; zero‑carbon new buildings by 2021, rising to Passivhaus by 2025.
  - Circular economy law: phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; right‑to‑repair; 70% recycling target.
  - Nature recovery targets; 60m trees/year; peatland and marine protection; £5bn flood programme; sustainable farming reform.
  - Transport: Clean Air Act; all new cars/vans electric by 2030; more ULEZs; rail electrification by 2035; fare freeze for a parliament; expand light rail, buses, cycling/walking; fix fares and access.

- Health, social care and public health
  - +1p on Income Tax raising £7bn/year for NHS and social care; £10bn capital; plan for a dedicated Health and Care Tax; integrate services and end automatic tendering.
  - Mental health: new waiting‑time standards; 24/7 crisis care; perinatal support; free prescriptions for chronic conditions; student mental health charter; tighter gambling rules.
  - Prevention: obesity strategy; right to clean air; minimum unit pricing for alcohol; PrEP on NHS; decriminalise abortion UK‑wide with safe access zones; drug policy reform including a regulated cannabis market.

- Social security, housing and communities
  - Reform Universal Credit: first payment in 5 days; end two‑child limit and benefit cap; higher work allowances incl. second earner; replace sanctions with incentive‑based approach; abolish bedroom tax; align LHA with rents; reinstate Independent Living Fund; right to food; end fuel poverty by 2025.
  - Pensions: retain triple lock; remedy for women born in the 1950s.
  - Housing: build 300,000 homes/year incl. 100,000 for social rent; zero‑carbon standards; Rent‑to‑Own; longer tenancies; licensing; curb second homes; end rough sleeping; repeal Vagrancy Act.
  - Rural/coastal: bus and rural services funds; universal superfast broadband and wider mobile coverage; coastal change fund.

- Policing, justice and rights
  - £1bn for community policing; public‑health approach to serious violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; reform stop and search; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local boards.
  - Reduce reoffending: more prison officers; presumption against short sentences; decriminalise possession for personal use; Women’s Justice Board; fair disclosure rules; strong rehabilitation on release.
  - Rights: protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; restore Legal Aid (£500m); halt police facial recognition; data/AI ethics code; no‑fault divorce; cohabiting rights; comprehensive equality measures incl. gender recognition reform, BSL Act, period poverty action, parental leave reform and pay‑gap transparency.

- Immigration and asylum
  - End the hostile environment; 28‑day limit on detention; move visa policy out of the Home Office to specialist departments; flexible work and post‑study visas; lower/waived fees; fair family rules.
  - Asylum: right to work after 3 months; resettle 10,000 vulnerable refugees annually and 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years; faster, higher‑quality decisions; free English lessons; longer move‑on period.

- Foreign policy and defence
  - Support multilateral institutions; maintain 0.7% aid with stronger focus on climate, gender and human rights; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; tighter arms export controls (including suspensions to rights‑abusing conflicts).
  - Parliamentary votes on military action; NATO 2% spending; bolster cyber capabilities; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent (reduced fleet, altered posture).
